title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of political impersonation carried out with generative video. A candidate was depicted saying words she never said, and the fabricated clips were published to a public social platform by the opposing campaign. The failure sits at the point of publication rather than in the model itself: the videos were made and posted deliberately, so no automated safeguard inside a generation tool was the last line of defence. Catching it would have required the platform or the poster to label or withhold synthetic depictions of a real person, and the reporting does not say whether any such label was applied.

The harm here is reputational and electoral rather than technical. The fabricated statements were attributed to a named person and distributed under a real campaign's account, which is the mechanism by which a deepfake converts into a defamation claim. The cease-and-desist letter asserts that publishing false statements to harm reputation risks violating state defamation law. That is an allegation by one side's attorney, not a court finding, and no ruling, damages or removal order is established in the reporting.

What is not established is whether the videos were intended to deceive viewers, whether any platform acted on them, and whether the legal threat produced any change in the posting. The response from the opposing campaign, including a further AI video, is reported as a reaction, not as an admission of any legal position.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI-generated deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including claims about corruption, illegal immigrants, and Communists. The letter points to a video shared on Aug. 4 and says Cooke never made those statements.

Cooke's attorney, Ben Stafford, wrote on Sept. 30 that Van Orden risks violating state defamation law by publishing false statements to harm Cooke's reputation. The letter says Cooke's attorneys are monitoring Van Orden's social media and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden's campaign called Cooke's action a tantrum, and Van Orden responded with another AI video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!"
